dependencies.reason: uses its router, error envelope and request conventions, and implements the cursor pagination those conventions define
records the opening credential's identity and type from its authentication
uses its workspace record and access decision, and hooks into its archive and delete to end active sessions

tasks.title: Build the cursor pagination every paged route will use
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the pagination test file, and confirm they fail
Implement an opaque cursor that encodes a position in an ordered result and is tamper-evident, so one this service did not issue cannot be made to return a wrong page
Return next_cursor and has_more with every page, with next_cursor null exactly on the last page
Continue from a returned cursor so that reading to the end yields every row exactly once in the requested order, proved by a generative test over row counts, page sizes and both orders
Refuse a malformed, truncated or unissued cursor with 400 and no rows
Expose the facility so that package 12 and any later paged route reuse it rather than writing another

tasks.title: Open sessions idempotently
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the session routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Define the session and usage tables, with a migration the second target runs too
Implement the open: record the workspace, run, node, archetype, model and metadata with the opening credential's id and type, and answer 201
Answer 200 with the existing session when the id already exists and the caller may read its workspace, recording no second session
Require write access to the named workspace whatever its status, so a member is refused and an archived workspace is still allowed
Refuse a missing or empty workspace_slug with 400, and a workspace the caller may not see or a replayed id belonging to one with 404

tasks.title: Complete sessions and record their usage
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the session routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Admit the complete and usage routes to the session's creator and to an admin token alone, refusing the workspace's owner when they are not the creator
Close an active session with completed, failed or timeout, and answer 200 with an already terminal session unchanged
Record a usage report against an active session and include it in the session's token summary
Refuse an invalid status and the status terminated with 400, a caller who is not the creator with 403 not session owner, an unknown session with 404 and a concurrent close with 409
Refuse a usage report with no model with 400, one for a session that is not active with 409, and one with a negative token count with 422, writing nothing

tasks.title: Read sessions and their usage
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the session routes' test files, and confirm they fail

List sessions newest first by default with their token summaries, honouring the workspace, run, status, credential type and start-time filters, the order, and a page size defaulting to 50 and capped at 500
Read one session with its token summary, answering 404 for an unknown id
List a session's usage records with a page size defaulting to 100 and capped at 1000, computing the totals over every record of the session so they do not change with the page size
Require read access and an active workspace for every read, answering 403 workspace access denied to anyone else and to every caller of an archived workspace
Refuse an invalid cursor with 400

tasks.title: Aggregate a workspace's cost
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the cost test files, and confirm they fail
Aggregate the workspace's sessions' usage over a period, grouped by day, session or model, defaulting to day and to the last 24 hours
Answer with the workspace, the period, the totals and the breakdown, with the totals equal to the sum of the breakdown and agreeing with the usage records
Refuse a start that is not before the end, and a grouping outside day, session and model, with 400
Require read access and an active workspace, answering 403 workspace access denied otherwise

tasks.title: End sessions when their workspace is retired
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the session lifecycle integration test file, and confirm they fail
At the archive and delete of package 03, end every active session of the workspace with the status terminated
Leave sessions that were already terminal unchanged, and sessions of other workspaces untouched
Confirm no session of the retired workspace remains active afterwards
Leave a documented place for package 12 to record the force-closed event for each session ended

tasks.title: Verify recording, reporting and retirement against a running deployment
steps: Add the three smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment, or skips with a message naming the missing deployment

Trace 11-PATH-1: the open records the real credential identity of package 02, the usage reports reach the real store, and the read returns totals computed over every record through the pagination facility
Trace 11-PATH-2: the cost route reads the same usage records the session route reports, so the two agree rather than being computed twice
Trace 11-PATH-3: package 03's archive reaches the session termination, and the subsequent read is refused by the active-workspace rule rather than by a stale status

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the pagination facility is used by the session list, the usage list and nothing writes its own cursor; the access rule is used by every read route; and the termination is reached from the real archive and delete
Grep src/session/, src/paging/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the session and cost conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
the session, usage and cost routes answer as docs/prd/api.md specifies against a running deployment, cursor paging included
